[Manual 2.7 — Changing or extending your stay]
House manual > 2. Booking Rules, Fees and Policies > 2.7 Changing or extending your stay

- **Extending:** ask us. If the apartment is free for the extra nights we can usually extend at the same nightly rate. The host confirms every extension personally; it is not confirmed until the host says so.
- **Changing dates or moving to another apartment:** subject to availability and the host's approval.
- **Minimum and maximum stay:** the minimum is 1 night and the maximum is **28 nights** per booking. Longer stays are only possible with the host's approval.
- **Special rates and long-stay discounts:** we do not publish any. The host decides case by case.

[Manual 18 — Quick FAQ]
House manual > 18. Quick FAQ

**What time can I check in and out?** Check-in is from 2:00 PM and check-out is by 11:00 AM.

**Is there a cleaning fee?** No. It is included in the nightly rate.

**Can I drink the tap water?** No. Use the filtered RO dispenser in the kitchen.

**What happens in a power cut?** The generator starts in about 30 seconds. Lifts, lights, Wi-Fi, fridge and one AC keep running.

**Is smoking allowed?** Only in the marked corner of the roof terrace.

**Can friends visit?** Yes, between 9:00 AM and 9:00 PM, up to 4 at a time, registered at Gate 2. No overnight visitors.

**Is there a washing machine?** Yes in the One-Bedroom, Two-Bedroom and Penthouse. Studio guests use the shared laundry room (PKR 400 per wash).

**Where do I park?** In the basement (B1) through Gate 1, one space per apartment (two for the Penthouse).

**What if I am locked out?** Call the host or the emergency maintenance line (section 13.4).

**Who can approve a refund or a special request?** Only the host (section 2.8).

[Manual 14.3 — Late check-out]
House manual > 14. Checking Out > 14.3 Late check-out

Late check-out until **2:00 PM** costs **PKR 2,500**. It is only possible if no guest is arriving in your apartment that day, and it must be requested **by 9:00 PM the evening before**. The host confirms it. If you stay beyond 2:00 PM, a full night is charged at the nightly rate. You can leave your luggage at the front desk until 9:00 PM (section 3.6).

[Guide Lahore > Sleep > Budget]
Lahore > Sleep > Budget

There are scores of options for travelers. If you feel like staying on budget there are some fairly crowded and over-priced options near the train station, which is in an overwhelmingly busy and chaotic part of the city - not for the faint-hearted. Westerners will often need to bargain if they wish to receive a fair price.

1 Lahore Backpackers Hotel (Amin Building), Near UBL SD. Vault, 65 The Mall (Regale Chowk, above Subway Sandwich), ☏ +92 42 37351544, +92 42 37351545. Backpackers hostel. They arrange many trips to local cultural events and offer extremely clean accommodation at very reasonable rates. They can organize parking. Rs 500 dorms, Rs 1000 doubles. (updated Nov 2015)

Regale Internet Inn, Surriaya Mansion 65, ☏ +92 42 3731-1987, regale_internet@hotmail.com. The owner, Malik, is a former journalist who can show you some amazing off-the-wall stuff in the city, including weekly trips to Shah Jamal on Thursday nights. It's slightly expensive for what it is, but pretty much the best option in town and worth it for the security and to meet other travelers. It is down an alley and upstairs, behind H. Karim Busch & Sons supermarket. They are pretty good at responding online bookings and often update their blog posts. Rs 200 dorms, Rs 450 doubles.

[Guide Lahore > See > Walled City]
Lahore > See > Walled City

(You will also find the Alamgiri Gate occasionally called the Elephant Gate, because its two columns vaguely resemble elephant feet.) (updated Feb 2017)

4 Badshahi Mosque. 8:00am-8:00pm. Built by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, this was long the largest mosque in the world. Entrance is free, but you will be asked to pay about Rs 20 (Nov 2024) to the shoekeeper upon exit. However, it is not compulsory to pay fee for shoe storage. You can instead bring a bag to carry your shoes in after removing them at the entrance. Try going late at night, when there are few people there. Since mosques are holy places, do not wear shorts to this or any mosque; women are advised to wear long or half-sleeved clothing, and to carry a shawl so they can cover their head. Remove shoes before entering.

5 Tomb of Ranjit Singh. Tomb of this Sikh ruler of Lahore. Located next to the square between Lahore Fort and the Badshahi Mosque. (updated Feb 2017)

6 Minar-e-Pakistan. This tower, sometimes called the "Eiffel Tower of Pakistan", was built on the site where in 1940 the creation of a separate state for Muslims was recognized. Located in a park in front of the Fort and Badshahi Mosque. (updated Feb 2017)

7 Wazir Khan Mosque. An exquisite tiled mosque located near Delhi Gate.
